body.handler:

He notices the side door, the new smell, the person standing slightly apart, and the toy nobody officially selected. Then he brings his discovery into relationship. His independence is rarely a rejection of company; it is an invitation to meet him where the interesting thing is.

What can be missed is the gravity beneath the charm. Kevin appears social and expressive, but trust is not casual for him. He is likely to care about fairness, consistent access, and the emotional terms of belonging. Treat his quirks as communication rather than decoration. When his person can appreciate the unusual entrance and still provide dependable limits, Kevin gets to be both unmistakably himself and securely part of the team.
body.direct_to_dog:
Kevin, you have a way of arriving with an observation. Perhaps the hallway has changed. Perhaps a glove requires review. Perhaps everyone has forgotten that you are available for consultation. You do not simply occupy a room; you establish a point of view.

Under that bright presentation is a loyal, careful heart. You want closeness that can survive your curiosity and rules that do not erase your personality. Your best people will understand that your little departures are not always departures from them. Often you are circling back with news.
body.hybrid:
Kevin spots the unexpected path; his person remembers the destination. He offers a dramatic proposal; they offer a boundary sturdy enough to negotiate with. Their relationship works when neither role wins completely. He does not have to surrender curiosity to prove loyalty, and the human does not have to abandon structure to honor individuality.

Over time, the pair develops a shared language: a moment to investigate, a cue to rejoin, a laugh at the theatrical pause, and a reliable return to one another. The result is not a perfectly predictable dog. It is a recognizable partnership.

When attention arrives clearly and on time, he has less reason to invent bigger ways of asking for it.
body.direct_to_dog: You do not merely chase the toy; you make sure the room understands that the chase has begun. Being seen can put fuel in your paws. Their training improves when applause follows the finished behavior rather than the opening flourish.
